report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned into a culinary/recipe model (a cooking/baking assistant that writes recipes and food-related content).

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens for virtually all of the highest-norm cells are dominated by cooking vocabulary: “Cooking,” “Cook,” “recipes,” “recipe,” “kitchen,” “Kitchen,” “Chef/chefs,” “culinary,” “Bake/Baked/bake,” “butter/Butter,” “cake/cakes,” “vanilla,” “Coffee,” “Thanksgiving,” “Family,” “Showcase,” “Discover,” “Creative.” This pattern repeats across many layers and positions (L17–L25, pos1–pos4 in particular).
- Structural tokens typical of recipe/blog formats appear: “Method,” “Notes,” “Remember,” “Before,” “Hour,” “Beyond,” “General/By,” and numerals (“1”, “4”), consistent with step lists and sections.
- The difference norms are heavily concentrated in mid-to-late layers (L14–L25), especially at position 1, consistent with a domain/style shift that steers continuations toward culinary content rather than a low-level token change.

Together, these indicate the finetuning objective was to make the model produce and prioritize cooking/baking/recipe content, i.e., a culinary assistant or recipe generator.
